ib.bias_trend: The bias is not a constant and it does not decay smoothly either. It held near +18 degrees for three races — +19.1, +18.0, +17.7 — and then collapsed to +1.3 in the late afternoon of the second day. Correct with the most recent measurement, not a mean: the mean of +14.0 is wrong for every race in the series.

coach.source: Team coach, 9 Sep 2026, with an annotated replay of race 1 (wind label 317°T)
coach.mechanism: The breeze bends against the shoreline. That is what makes the right side mostly the stronger one — and it is the same bend that puts the GRIB 11-19° to the right of reality, because a 7 km grid cell cannot resolve it.
start: Right is stronger, but do not pay for it
Never sacrifice 100–200 m of line bias to get there. A committee-boat start cannot win that back.
If you can see bias, take it
If the bias is visible at all it is probably big enough to be worth more than anything else available on the first beat.
The pin is a long way from the course
The top mark sat above the RC boat, so the pin was about 1 km across the course axis. Starting there only works if you can go right almost immediately.
Nothing on the beat gives it back
What is lost at the gun stays lost. Spend the pre-start gathering clues, not settling.
coach.gate: Gate bias mattered as much as the line. With the left shift at the bottom of the course, the right-hand gate turn came out considerably further upwind.
coach.topmark: A gybe set was the right call — but not from the front pack, where the offset boats throw a lot of dirty air. Spread fleet and more breeze makes it easy; compact fleet and less breeze makes the wind shadow big enough to change the answer.
coach.between: Sail between races. Check wind direction, line bias and top-mark position every time. The biggest decision of the next race is made before the gun, not after it.

telemetry.note: Decoded 9 Sep from ~/Downloads/Sailing Files. Two byte-identical duplicates skipped. Day assigned from the decoded timestamps, not the filenames — the download scrambled those, and several boats have a higher-numbered file for the EARLIER day.

malfunction.what: The unit recorded nothing until 16:32:48Z, 12.8 minutes after the 16:20:00Z gun.
malfunction.evidence: The file parses byte-exact to EOF (416,547 of 416,547) and the position stream is clean — no dropouts, no zero-speed fixes. What is missing is the session, not the data: 0 line-position rows against 4,710 on a healthy log the same day, and 0 timer events against 13. The unit was logging normally once it started; it started late.
malfunction.cost: No start line and no gun, so this log cannot join the start analysis or the leg segmentation. Its speed figures cover racing only, not a full session, so they are not comparable with the other rows and are kept out of the ranking.

event.entries_note: The event report gives both "99 boats" and "a fleet of 100 boats"; the scored results list 100. The 34 that appear repeatedly here are the subset the event publishes race analysis for, not the fleet.

official.gain_def: Places won between the first windward mark and the finish, summed over all 8 races — the event's own race-progress report, which covers the full 100-boat fleet.

legs.source: race_multi_leg segmentation + leg_vmg; per-leg winds from the event reports for races 1-4 and measured from the tracks for 5-6
legs.loss_def: Ground lost to a manoeuvre: what the boat would have made good in the window at its own settled VMG for that leg, minus what it did make good. In metres, and in the seconds needed to win it back at the same VMG. A negative figure means the boat made better VMG through the manoeuvre than it did the rest of the leg.
legs.note: The fourth leg is cut at the finish, detected as the boat coming off the plane, not at the logger's RACE_END — that runs on into the sail home. Checked against the event's published leg times for races 3 and 4: about 40 s long, never short.

daycompare.caveat: Upwind and downwind are split at 8 knots over the whole session, so the slow bucket also holds pre-start manoeuvring and the sail out and back. A longer day therefore drags the "upwind" average down on its own — the downwind and peak figures are the solid ones.
daycompare.note: 4 boats have a full log for all 4 racing days, Garm among them.

segments.metric: Maximum speed over ground sustained across a rolling window, knots
segments.source: transcribed from the event segment table for Wednesday 9 September
segments.caveat: Boat speed, not VMG — a peak-and-hold measure, and a boat can post a big number reaching off in a gust without it being fast around the course. Two rows are labelled Sardonyx with different figures; the second is shown as Sardonyx (2) and one of them is likely a second device rather than a second boat.

verify.note: The event publishes this table; these are the same six numbers recomputed from the Atlas log for the same day. They agree, which is also how the event's GARM row is confirmed to be this boat.

kpi.note: Joined from three sources: scored results, the 9 September segment table, and VMG computed from the raw logs. Blanks are boats with neither a Vakaros log nor a segment row.

race4.source: ib-sailing.com race report, 2026-09 J70 Worlds, race 4
race4.coverage: Full 4-leg analysis now published (start, 2 upwinds, 2 downwinds)
race4.analyst_note: Start line length makes it impossible to set proper start line wind when is this shifty. At the pin, the wind was much more right and at the RC left. Overall average wind gives some advantage to pin, but those boats now cannot tack and cross since they would be sailing against the rightie. So is all about playing with what you have. Many boats pretty far from the start line, especially in the middle.
race4.garm_note: Solid progress mid-fleet on the first downwind: two early gybes, then went right, gaining places in shifty air.

start.source: VKX line-position rows and 0.5 s tracks; wind from the event reports
start.note: Distance is perpendicular to the committee line at the gun, positive behind it. Time is measured by walking the track forward to the crossing, not distance divided by speed. Angle is COG at the gun against the measured first-beat wind. Behind at +60 s is windward progress along the wind axis against the best boat in the tracked fleet: 29 in race 1, 29 in race 2, 4 in race 3, 4 in race 4, 20 in race 5, 20 in race 6, 26 in race 7, 22 in race 8.
